name: How long does it take to replace kitchen cabinets?

mainEntity.name: How long does it take to replace kitchen cabinets?

acceptedAnswer.text: The physical tear-out and installation of new kitchen cabinets typically takes about three to five days, but the overall project timeline depends on the full scope of work. Removing old cabinets often reveals drywall issues, shifted framing, or plumbing and electrical lines that require coordination before new boxes can be hung. If your project includes new countertops, tile backsplashes, or floor adjustments, the entire renovation generally spans two to three weeks. Working with a hands-on general contractor who leads the carpentry, drywall, and finish work on-site helps minimize scheduling downtime between trade phases.
acceptedAnswer.description: Cabinet tear-out and installation typically takes 3 to 5 days, while full kitchen remodels involving counters, drywall, and tile usually take 2 to 3 weeks.
